entries.exactPassage: Here’s the tension: digital security requires resources—a smartphone for 2FA, money for a password manager, reliable internet to update software. Not everyone has these. If you cannot afford a paid password manager, use a free one. If you cannot use 2FA because you do not have a consistent phone number, use the strongest possible passwords and change them regularly. If you cannot update your software because of data costs, do it when you have Wi-Fi access. Do what you can with what you have. Partial security is better than no security. And here is the deeper truth: the biggest digital security risk is not technology. It is behavior. Clicking on links without thinking. Using public Wi-Fi for banking. Sharing passwords with friends. Ignoring software updates. The most sophisticated security system in the world cannot protect you from your own carelessness. Security is not a product. It is a practice.
entries.category: Authentication access and outdated rotation advice
entries.concern: MFA is treated as universally requiring a smartphone/stable number and routine password rotation as the alternative; behaviour receives sole blame.
entries.proposedWording: Use service-specific supported factors and protected recovery, unique strong passwords and changes after compromise/reuse as appropriate; routine arbitrary rotation is not an MFA substitute. Recognise system/provider failures and access constraints.

entries.exactPassage: Here’s the tension: the five forms of wealth are not independent. Financial wealth can protect health wealth—by paying for medical care. Time wealth can protect relational wealth—by creating space for the people you love. Health wealth enables everything—without it, the other forms are inaccessible. The forms are connected. Neglect one, and the others eventually suffer. Build all five, and they reinforce each other. The person who protects only their money may find they have nothing worth spending it on. The person who protects only their relationships may find they cannot support the people they love. The architect designs for integration. The operator protects the whole system—not just one part of it.
entries.concern: Without health the other forms are said to be inaccessible, which excludes meaningful disabled/chronically ill lives.
entries.proposedWording: Retain the reflective interconnection framework while recognising accessible relationships, experiences, purpose and dignity with illness or disability and appropriate support.
